_doc: Round 17 — the custom class. Everything here is the TUNING a point-buy character needs and nothing here is a copy of anything. The spell tier list itself is NOT in this file: js/classbuild.js derives it at load from data/classes.json and data/skills.json, because those two are already the source of truth for all 30 preset classes and a committed copy of them would drift the first time somebody adds a skill. See CLASSES.md, 'Where the tier list comes from'.
_wordingDoc: Round 21 — every blurb in this file is held to WORDING.md: name the thing rather than saying 'it', and give magnitude and duration as digits. The loadout blurbs quote js/weapons.js (WEAPON_PATTERNS reach and clock, WEAPON_TRAITS damage/armourBreak/backstab/guard/pierceLine, RANGED ranges and draw power, OFFHAND_DAMAGE, STAFF_CHARGE) and js/rpg.js (a wand's 34 m castRange). The element blurbs quote data/skills.json `statuses` carried through js/main.js `brandHit`, which hands the status 70% of the hit's damage as its power — so burn's 0.3/s over 5s is 0.3 x 5 x 0.7 = about 105% of the hit again. The companion blurbs quote data/enemies.json. Change one of those numbers and this file is wrong, so change this file too.
_customDoc: The synthetic class a custom build is injected as. `id` is what ends up in the save's `classId`, which is why it must never collide with one of the 30 real ones.

custom.name: Freelance
custom.hook: Nothing came with this class. Every spell on the bar was chosen.

_tierDoc: The six rungs, mirroring data/skills.json's `unlockAt`. A spell's TIER is the earliest rung any of the 30 classes hands it out on; a pick may only take a spell whose tier is at or below the rung being filled, which is the whole of the point-buy rule. The levels below are a cross-check, not a second source: js/classbuild.js asserts they match skills.json and throws if they do not, because two ladders that disagree is the bug this project keeps finding.

tiers.name: Opening
tiers.blurb: The spell you start the game holding, at level 1.

tiers.name: Sixth
tiers.blurb: Your 6th and last spell, unlocked at level 24.

_loadoutDoc: Every sensible pair of hands. `main` and `off` are weaponBase keys out of the shared items.json; `offArmour` is an off-hand ARMOUR base (a shield, a focus, a quiver) rather than a second weapon. `needsPerk` names a perk-forest keystone by its KEYSTONE id — a saved perk is the node id, so js/classbuild.js looks the node up through the forest rather than hard-coding one. `element` marks the loadouts that carry a branded caster and therefore get an element picker.

loadouts.name: Blade and Board
loadouts.blurb: A longsword at 3.0 m reach, a swing every 0.64s, and a shield to get in the way. The build that survives its own mistakes.

loadouts.name: Hammer and Board
loadouts.blurb: A hammer at 2.5 m reach, a swing every 0.66s, stripping 7% of the target's armour on every hit, behind a kite shield.

loadouts.name: Spear and Shield
loadouts.blurb: 4.0 m of reach behind a shield, and a thrust that runs through 2 bodies in a line.

loadouts.name: Javelin and Buckler
loadouts.blurb: Javelins thrown out to 28 m, landing in a 1.4 m splash every 0.75s, with a buckler in the free hand.

loadouts.name: Two Blades
loadouts.blurb: Two swords on two clocks, 2.8 m reach each. The off-hand sword deals 60% damage and never stops.

loadouts.name: Knife Pair
loadouts.blurb: 2.0 m reach and a strike every 0.34s — the fastest hands in the game — dealing 80% damage from the front and 2.2× damage from behind.

loadouts.name: Rapier and Knife
loadouts.blurb: Thrust, thrust, lunge at 3.3 m with a 10% chance to block, and a dagger for whatever closes the distance.

loadouts.name: Great Blade
loadouts.blurb: A 3.9 m sweep and a slow overhead every 0.88s, at 1.20× damage for taking both hands.

loadouts.name: Great Axe
loadouts.blurb: 3.6 m of cleave at 1.20× damage, opening a bleed on every cleave and stripping 5% of the target's armour per hit.

loadouts.name: Halberd
loadouts.blurb: 4.8 m of reach at 1.20× damage, and a thrust that runs through 3 bodies standing in a line.

loadouts.name: Quarterstaff
loadouts.blurb: A pole, not a wand: 3.5 m reach, a strike every 0.48s, and a 12% chance to block while the staff is held.

loadouts.name: Bow and Quiver
loadouts.blurb: A bow out to 46 m. A full 0.95s draw hits for 1.60× damage; loosed early the shot hits for 0.55×.

loadouts.name: Crossbow and Quiver
loadouts.blurb: Bolts out to 50 m at 1.80× damage, with 1.25s to crank the crossbow back between shots. No draw to hold.

loadouts.name: Wand and Focus
loadouts.blurb: A branded bolt out to 34 m, and a warded focus in the other hand.

loadouts.name: Wand and Tome
loadouts.blurb: Both hands casting out to 34 m, the off hand at 60% damage. No shield, so nothing to block with at all.

loadouts.name: Elemental Staff
loadouts.blurb: Swung, not aimed, and every swing carries the element you chose. A 1.40s charge casts at full damage; holding to 2.60s casts at 1.60× damage over 2× the area.

loadouts.name: Sceptre and Shield
loadouts.blurb: A sceptre that casts and still stands in the front rank: 2.5 m reach behind a shield, stripping 4% of the target's armour per hit.

loadouts.name: Two Two-Handers
loadouts.blurb: A two-handed sword and a two-handed axe at once, both at 1.20× damage, the off-hand axe at 60% of that. Only possible once the Doubled Grasp keystone is taken.

_elementDoc: What a branded caster may be attuned to. These are rpg.js's own CAST_ELEMENTS keys — js/classbuild.js checks each one resolves there, so a choice can never be an element the game does not have. The blurbs quote data/skills.json `statuses` at the power js/main.js `brandHit` hands them (70% of the hit's damage), stated as a TOTAL over the whole duration the way WORDING.md rule 2 requires.

elements.name: Flame
elements.blurb: A hit also sets Burning: about 105% of that hit's damage again, as fire damage, over 5s.

elements.name: Rime
elements.blurb: A hit also sets Chilled: the target moves 45% slower for 4s.

elements.name: Storm
elements.blurb: A hit also sets Shocked: the target takes 30% more damage from every source for 5s.

elements.name: Blight
elements.blurb: A hit also sets Poisoned: about 146% of that hit's damage again, as poison damage, over 8s.

elements.name: Gloom
elements.blurb: A hit also sets Cursed: the target takes 25% more damage and moves 15% slower for 8s.

elements.name: Arc
elements.blurb: Plain arcane damage. Arc is the 1 element that leaves no status on the target at all.

_armourDoc: What each armour tier puts on you at level 1. Base keys out of items.json, equipped exactly the way a preset class's `startingArmour` is.
_openingDoc: The one choice the user asked for by name: somebody to walk with you, or a crate and some money for the people who would rather be alone. A companion is a bestiary pet id out of data/enemies.json, so it is a real body with real numbers — and the blurbs below quote those numbers. The crate is rolled through rpg.loot the same way every chest in the game is — `floor` is the worst rarity it can hold, which is what makes 'three magic or better' a promise rather than a hope.

companions.name: A wolf
companions.blurb: 46 health, 5–9 damage a bite, one bite every 1.3s. Fast and fragile.

companions.name: A dire hound
companions.blurb: 78 health and 6 armour, 7–12 damage every 1.7s. The heavy one: walks in first and stays there.

companions.name: A hunting cat
companions.blurb: 40 health, 6–10 damage every 1.1s at 5.6 m/s. The fastest companion, and the one that reaches the casters.

companions.name: A bone thrall
companions.blurb: 2 thralls, 34 health and 4–7 damage each. Cheap and expendable.

companions.name: An ember familiar
companions.blurb: 30 health, 6–10 fire damage out to 24 m, and every hit sets Burning. Flies.

companions.name: A storm familiar
companions.blurb: 30 health, 6–10 lightning damage out to 26 m. Flies, and has the longest reach of the familiars.

companions.name: A spirit bear
companions.blurb: 110 health and 10 armour — the toughest companion — for 8–13 damage every 2s at 3.6 m/s.

companions.name: A clockwork sentry
companions.blurb: 60 health and 12 armour, 6–11 damage out to 30 m. Rolls along behind you and never needs feeding.

companions.name: A bound imp
companions.blurb: 42 health and 3 armour, 7–12 shadow damage out to 24 m.

crate.name: A Sealed Chest
crate.blurb: 3 items of magic quality or better, and 450 gold.

_lookDoc: Which of the 30 class looks a custom character borrows its body from before the appearance editor gets to it. Nothing but a starting point — Customize on the character step replaces the whole avatar.
